#1933. England versus Spain becoming a new 'clásico' as Leeds United keeper James Trafford announces himself on world stage

That's how widely-respected Spanish sports newspaper Marca described La Roja's rivalry with England following the Three Lions' stunning Sunday-best victory at the Metropolitano. High praise indeed.

That it is becoming one of the most absorbing and significant in world football is surely beyond doubt now.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In terms of beating the world champions, England have been here before. Back in November 2011, a screamer from Frank Lampard secured a Wembley victory against the feted Spanish, who were also European Championship holders at the same time.

This felt different. On that aforesaid occasion, England prevailed following a backs-to-the-wall performance which saw them pinned back in their own half for long spells against dominant opponents. They converted one of just two chances that came their way.

By contrast, Sunday saw those in white subjugate Spain with an elite showing.

Certainly for 65 to 70 minutes, the hosts' much-vaunted midfield—Arsenal duo Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, alongside Fabián Ruiz and Alex Baena—were suffocated by England's high press.

It was an intense game plan executed 'with the precision of a master tailor' in the words of Marca. Ruiz and Merino both got the hook at half-time.

The narrative only changed when Elliot Anderson received his marching orders.

The hosts roared back and things became undeniably hairy in the final quarter. But unlike against Argentina in Atlanta in July, Thomas Tuchel's substitutions did not see England adopt a defensive straitjacket.

Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on as the visitors focused on staying higher up the pitch, if at all possible, amid serious late pressure from Spain.

It ended in a merited 3-2 win for the English. In three of the last four meetings between these two, a team has triumphed by the odd goal in five.

England triumphed by the same scoreline and in similar fashion to their previous visit to Spain back in October 2018 - in another Nations League encounter played out in Seville, this time. Again, they achieved success by being proactive as opposed to parking the bus.

Fabulous counter-attacking strikes from Raheem Sterling (2) and Marcus Rashford put the visitors 3-0 up to silence the Spanish hordes. It was the prelude to a strong home fightback in the second half, but no victory.

On this occasion, England's physical and tactical dominance was even more sustained and their third goal, scored by Ben White on 57 minutes, finished off a move of the highest order.

For too long in the past, certainly before that 2018 occasion in Seville, England had been cowed on their visits to Spain. In their previous four matches, all defeats, they failed to score. Ever since Gary Lineker, then at Barcelona, struck all four goals in a stunner at Madrid's Bernebeu Stadium in February 1987.

England have now regained the full respect of international football's undoubted success story of the current century. The team who, alongside France, are the current benchmark for all other nations.

Sunday night was undeniably sweetened by the fact that Spain relinquished their magnificent 44-game unbeaten sequence in the process.

That run included a 2-1 win over England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin and this summer’s World Cup.

Spain's previous defeat was back in March 2023 against Scotland in Glasgow.

On an evening when the usual suspects came to the party in the shape of Jude Bellingham, whose pass for White's goal was delectable and Harry Kane, others also accepted their invites.

What a night for Leeds's James Trafford for instance. His fantastic double save late on to deny Fer Lopez and Aymeric Laporte announced his arrival on the world stage.

It presents Tuchel with a genuine headache - a welcome one, that said - regarding who will be his bonafide No 1 in 2027.

The battle between Trafford and Jordan Pickford is now a proper fight. It's not quite Peter Shilton versus Ray Clemence levels in the 1970s and early 80s just yet, but it might be heading in that direction. Tellingly, Trafford started both Nations League games against Spain, as opposed to his Everton rival.

Remember, remember the month of November? England will.

Sunday's success was a statement win of the ilk of 2015 when they beat the French 2-0 at Wembley and a decade earlier, in the same month, when a late brace from Michael Owen saw them triumph 3-2 against bitter foes Argentina, in Geneva of all places. Let's hope on this occasion, they build on it.

#1931. I won't do a Mauricio Pochettino! Thomas Tuchel insists there is 'zero chance' he will walk out on England for a Premier League job - but admits he misses club football

Published: 14:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 15:19 EST, 11 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel will stay loyal to England until the end of his contract at the 2028 European Championship but admits that he does miss the regular thrill of club management.

As Mauricio Pochettino prepares to activate a release clause with the USA national team to take the Manchester United job, England boss Tuchel has vowed to ignore all outside offers until the end of his deal with England.

‘There is no release clause,’ said Tuchel. ‘I signed the contract. I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.’

After that Tuchel said that he is open-minded.

Asked whether he could stay longer with England, he said with a smile that: ‘I am open to everything.’

The chances are, though, that England will be looking for a new coach once the 2028 Euros are done.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he misses club football - but won't walk out on England

He enjoys the buzz of managing 50 matches per season but is contracted until 2028

‘I miss the 50 [club] matches a season,’ Tuchel said. ‘I miss those two minutes when everything is done. You go out the two minutes before the first whistle goes. It's like the best two minutes.

‘Everything is done. You're in a full stadium. Lights are on and you're just so excited and you're part of it.

‘That's actually the two minutes where I realise how lucky and how grateful I am. Then the whistle goes, and then you're just in the tunnel again, trying to win the game for your team.’

Tuchel originally signed a short-term deal through to last summer’s World Cup but extended it until the Euros in the months before the tournament that ended with a semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Asked if there was ‘zero chance’ of him leaving before the end of his contract, he said: ‘I would say so.

‘First of all, I'm very grateful for what I have here because I know how rare it is to be in love with your team and to have the trust and to be able to work freely with your coaching staff, which I am.

‘I love my group of players. I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things.

Pochettino is set to become the new manager of Manchester United, replacing Michael Carrick

‘So, it's a lot. And I know how to appreciate it a lot.

‘It's in a good place. I'm in a good place. I'm desperate to win the Nations League and to play and try to win the Euros.’

England face Croatia at Wembley tonight in the Nations League before heading to Madrid for their final group game against Spain on Sunday. If England win both matches, they will top their group ahead of next March’s quarter-finals. At the very least they should progress as a second placed team.

The four teams emerging from next spring’s quarters will play Nations League semi-finals and final in one country next summer. With a venue yet to be chosen by UEFA, the FA are expected to throw their hat into the ring as a prospective host.

Tuchel has spoken before about the struggles England sometimes have in taking training performances on to the pitch and agreed that hosting the Nations League latter stages could act as a decent warm up before the challenges of playing a big tournament in front of a home crowd a year later.

‘The Nations League helps in general for us and I think to have it here could be exciting,’ Tuchel said.

‘It would be nice to have it here. So first of all, we need to reach the final before we play.

‘Playing at home is a challenge. It should be a home advantage when we go to the Euros and it should not become a home disadvantage that we feel in our brain.

‘It should be exciting and that's why it's also important what we are building at the moment and how the team plays.’

#1929. Watch: Arsenal star Ben White confronted amid heated tunnel bust-up during Spain vs England

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal stars found themselves at the centre of a dispute as England and Spain players clashed at half-time of their Nations League showdown.

Gunners defensive duo Ben White and Ezri Konsa were on the scoresheet for the Three Lions, helping their side to a famous 3-2 win away in Spain.

England, however, had to see out the final 30 minutes with a man disadvantage as Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson was shown a red card for fouling Lamine Yamal inside the box.

The other major talking point in the Spanish capital was an incident that occurred at half-time, when White clashed with Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz as the pair walked off the pitch.

Martin Zubimendi also attempted to play peacemaker after initially getting involved, conversing with Konsa as the huddle moved towards the tunnel.

A sixth Arsenal player was close by, as Mikel Merino - moments away from being hauled off at half-time - watched on as the argument fizzled out.

There were a total of eight Arsenal players involved in the matchday squads for both nations. Eberechi Eze was an unused sub on the England bench, with his club teammate Myles Lewis-Skelly introduced in the second half as Tuchel looked to see out victory for the Three Lions.

Hassell will step up while the Reds work towards appointing a new CEO.

A Reds statement read: “We know supporters will want reassurance as we head into a busy and important period on and off the pitch, so we want to be clear about how the club will be run in the interim, and what happens next.

"Bobby Hassell will take charge of the footballing side of the club on an interim basis.

A former Reds captain who made almost 300 appearances for the club, Bobby knows Barnsley Football Club inside out. He will work closely with head coach Daniel Stendel and his staff, and will lead our preparations for the January transfer window alongside the wider recruitment team.

#1926. Spain boss Luis de la Fuente issues warning after Nations League defeat to England

Luis de la Fuente has stated the “best is yet to come” from Spain following their loss to England.

England’s 3-2 victory away in Madrid on Sunday evening ended Spain’s run of 43 straight games without defeat, handing the World Cup winners their first loss since March 2024.

Under De La Fuente, Spain have won a European Championship, a World Cup and a Nations League title in 2023 - as well as reaching the final of the latter in 2025.

However, defeat to England means that Spain will enter the quarter-finals stage of the 2026-27 Nations League as an unseeded runner-up, potentially setting up a showdown with France in March next year.

Reflecting on the game, De La Fuente said: “In the first 30 minutes, they knocked us out of our rhythm and were better than us. After that, we fought back, and I thought we were going to get the draw.

“But I’ll use a phrase that I’ve used before when we were unbeaten: ‘The best is yet to come’.”

De La Fuente also shared his belief that England approached the game in Madrid as a ‘final’, with Spain not as motivated for the game - which allowed the Three Lions to ‘trample’ over La Roja.

"The fact that the whole world wants to beat Spain is a great feeling,” he added. “This was a 'final', and in this type of game, you have to be spot on, in great shape, and if not, then an opponent like England, France, Portugal or Italy can trample all over you.”

The Spanish head coach went on to state that his side’s ambitions of winning the Nations League remained in place, with his side ‘determined’ to make amends.

He continued: "We'll try to be exactly the same in defeat as we were in victory. Okay, we haven't often tasted defeat, but we stay proud; we stay determined - in March, we're in the quarter-finals, and we'll go to those knockouts with the intention of winning, and winning the tournament."

#1924. Worthing Women: Make Mackay-ne a double!

Nicole Mackay’s brace made it three goals in two games for her and a second successive win for Worthing Women, as they saw off Aylesford at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium.

After last week’s epic cup comeback at Camden, teenage starlet Hattie Rainey made her full debut while Ruby Murdock also came into the starting eleven; meaning that Skye Birkinshaw and Cristie Pritchard began on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barely had supporters sat in their seats than the aforementioned Mackay got the home team off and running, just three minutes in.

Seizing on  a loose ball on the edge of the eighteen yard area, the in-form striker drilled low and hard into Aylesford ‘keeper Sade Rider’s bottom right-hand corner, to open the scoring in emphatic fashion.

Although a very different picture might have been painted had the Rebels's netminder Sian Woods not denied a clean through Leigha Bradding-Butler not once but twice, to deny the visitor’s top scorer a seventh strike of a prolific campaign.

Still inside the opening ten minutes, Mackay came the width of the crossbar away from extending the host’s advantage. Dusting herself down and stepping up to take a free-kick she herself had won, the ball cannoned back off the frame of the goal, with Jess Richardson landing the rebound on top of the net.

The game settled into a more even contest for some time after that, as Worthing pressed forward in search of a second before the break, with Aylesford looking dangerous on the counter-attack.

Approaching the half-time interval, an audible sigh of relief reverberated around Woodside Road via Immy Armstrong - a threat from her set-pieces - firing narrowly over the target from inside the penalty area.

The sun then broke through the clouds on a pleasant November afternoon; similar to the way in which Aliyah Sheridan did when gifted possession by the homester’s otherwise solid last line of defence. Woods redeemed herself via a strong parry to her left of Sheridan’s subsequent shot.

One final opportunity before the change of ends fell to visiting Skipper Ami Burnham, only for Woods to keep her out by way of another excellent stop.

It’s tight at the bottom of the London & South East Prem but it was the Reds who headed into the interval with a precious one-goal lead.

Worthing continued to probe and were rewarded just shy of the hour mark, thanks to the persistence of Mackay. Although it was centre-half Ella Terry who got the ball rolling, courtesy of a wonderful switch of play from the middle of the park out to the roving Richardson on the right flank. The winger then found a well-placed Mackay to test Rider in the travellers’ net, with the Kent club’s custodian unable to prevent the Rebel’s number nineteen from overtaking Amber Hazlewood as leading markswoman in a red (occasionally lilac) shirt.

Some fine build-up laid the foundations for a possible third not long afterwards, when a Hattie Rainey pass went from a central position to wide on the right again, releasing the rapid Richardson to, ultimately, find Mackay once more, with the forward teeing up Neve McEvaddy for a long-range piledriver which saw Rider pull off a terrific save.

Goalscorer nearly turned provider three-quarters of the way into the contest but neither Richardson nor Annie Gracey could apply the finishing  touch to a dangerous-looking delivery.

Almost instantly, the visiting Blues hit back via a neat move of their own, culminating in half-time substitute Kara Richardson forcing Woods to hold on.

Ten to go and another excellent long ball from Terry resulted in some equally impressive hold-up play by the recently-introduced Paige Baker-Carroll, providing Richardson with an opening that she couldn’t quite keep down.

Not over the line yet though, the home side were reminded of the threat carried by Aylesford when Bradding-Bulter’s corner eventually led to Kara Richardson drawing a one-handed stop out of Woods, at the (in)expense of another flag-kick.

Time was running out for the girls from the Garden of England and Armstrong was quick to pounce on Pritchard's pass to fellow replacement Megan Gates; although the final flourish from twenty yards failed to test Woods between the home posts.

Fittingly, Worthing’s brightly-clad netminder had the last word on proceedings, as she added to her collection of wonder saves by frustrating Sheridan with only a few short minutes of normal time to play.

That would, indeed, be that and three vital points stayed at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium to move the Rebels up to ninth in the table, ahead of another tough test at bottom-of-the-table and fellow Sussex side Eastbourne Borough next Sunday.

#1919. HARRY KANE INTERVIEW: England captain opens up on having an 'ego', the secret behind Ballon d'Or glory, the 'tough' moments with his country - and why he isn't finished yet

Published: 14:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 16:11 EST, 11 November 2026

Harry Kane is contemplating his ego. England’s humble superstar, believes the outside world at least, does not have one. He laughs when reminded of his endearing habit of fiddling with his suit buttons during his Ballon d’Or acceptance speech.

But there must, surely, be one example beneath the modest exterior when he descends into a diva?

‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!’ he returns. ‘But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

Kane does have an ego, only it is measured in goals and self-improvement, not vanity and self-indulgence. He has the records because he wants the records, and he wants them more than all of his rivals. He played more games and scored more goals than Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal last season. After his 126th cap against Croatia tonight, he would have played more games and scored more goals than any player in England’s history. He wants those records to stand, too. Ego, you see.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ says Kane, as we chat at England’s base at the Tottenham Hotspur training ground. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record (currently 91) is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!’

It’s better than good, Harry. It is hard to believe now, but Kane was billed as a one-season wonder after his 31-goal breakthrough campaign at Tottenham 11 years ago. He remembers that, just like he does rejection by Arsenal aged eight years old, his missed penalty against France at World Cup 2022, the loan spell at Norwich when he was demoted to the reserves and the loan at Leicester when he sat alone in his flat and wondered if he was good enough for the Premier League.

England captain Harry Kane has admitted he has 'an ego to be the best' after winning the Ballon d'Or

‘I’ve had to prove people wrong my whole career,’ he says. 'If someone tells me I can’t do something, it motivates me to do it more. You look at all the great athletes, Tom Brady and that unwavering mentality to be the best. Maybe with me, because I’m a calm person and you don’t see the ego of some of these great players, it doesn’t mean I don’t want it as much as everyone else. It doesn’t mean I don’t put in the work and drive myself and everyone around me to be the best.

‘Getting released that early (by Arsenal) and proving them wrong. Proving my early coaches at Tottenham wrong, who I wasn’t playing as much under. Loan moves that didn’t go well. The World Cup in Qatar, missing that penalty was a really tough moment for me. After that, I scored the next 30 penalties! It’s the same thing, “I’m going to show them”, using all the negative stuff as motivation to push me to another level.’

Then there was Euro 2024, when Kane was substituted in the final defeat by Spain after an hour. The popular opinion went that his best days were behind him and England needed a new striker. He has since scored 25 goals from 27 international games. So much for the decline.

‘It was tough, getting taken off in a final,’ he says. ‘There was so much talk (before the final) around, “Maybe Harry shouldn't start”. I was like, “Well hang on a minute, I'm doing my best for the team here”.

‘I scored three goals and was joint for the Golden Boot. It wasn't like there were many other players doing crazy stuff that I wasn't doing. But from my own standards, I know I probably didn't quite reach the level that I could have. I don't think the team reached the level that we could have. After that, my position was under pressure. That motivated me to make sure that it wasn't. I was going to have to do even more to keep my place. From that moment, you've seen an improvement in me.’

Spend time with Kane, even just half an hour, and you realise he isn’t done yet.

’In football, you’ve never completed it,’ says the Bayern Munich star. ‘No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better. While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

You could never accuse Kane of not giving his all. His ego, the best kind of ego, would never allow anything else. England's greatest player is the diva who makes only demands of himself.

Two years after winning their League C group to return to the second tier, Northern Ireland go into Tuesday’s match away to Hungary knowing they will be elevated to League A if they avoid defeat in Budapest.

The prospect of moving to the top tier of European football is a huge prize to put in front of this young side.

The 22-year-old Kelly’s most memorable moment in international football to date came with his fine goal in a 3-1 friendly defeat by France in June. Competitive fixtures against nations of that calibre would be the norm in League A.

“I think that’s a big incentive,” Kelly said. “It’ll just put us in a really good place if we can top the group, that’ll be a really strong finish to the campaign.

“Playing against teams like France, England, Spain, that would be good to test yourself at that level, to play against them more often and kind of see where we are.”

Northern Ireland will have to deal with two key suspensions in Budapest, with manager Michael O’Neill needing to watch from the sidelines after picking up a touchline ban, while striker Jamie Donley – who has travelled to Hungary – is also out after getting his second booking.

Kelly said he was not worried about O’Neill’s ban.

“Not much changes,” he said. “We’ll just have our game plan ready and go in and try to produce that,” he said. “We’ll just be ready to play the game.”

Donley’s suspension could offer a bigger role to Kelly with O’Neill weighing how to rejig his attacking options without the man who has led the line throughout this campaign.

“We’ve been working on it now,” Kelly said. “We’re not 100 per cent sure who is going to do that yet. Jamie will be a big miss for us but we’ve got a good squad and whoever’s called upon will be able to go in there and try to replicate what he’s been doing really well for us.”

#1917. Thomas Tuchel and Spain manager agree on England verdict after famous Nations League win

England goalkeeper James Trafford has been singled out for praise from both managers after the heroic 3-2 win over Spain.

Thomas Tuchel’s side finished top of their Nations League group above the world champions on goal difference after they avenged September’s 3-2 defeat at Wembley with victory by the same scoreline in Madrid.

England played the last half an hour with 10 men following Elliot Anderson’s red card.

Tuchel handed Jordan Pickford and Trafford two matches each during the last international break and again split their game time, with the Everton stopper playing in Thursday’s 2-1 win over Croatia and Trafford coming into the team against Spain.

The Leeds shot-stopper made a string of crucial saves late in the game as 10-man England held on for a famous win that brought an end to Spain’s 43-match unbeaten run.

Trafford’s double save to deny Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte was particularly eye-catching, and his team-mates immediately mobbed him to praise him for those smart stops in added time.

The performance of the 24-year-old - vying with Pickford for the No1 shirt ahead of Euro 2028 - drew praise not only from Tuchel but also from his opposite number, the Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente.

“We did generate some chances, but England’s goalkeeper produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes,” De la Fuente said afterwards.

“I want to say how fantastic England were on the night,” he added.

Trafford’s own head coach was similarly impressed by the Leeds man’s influence on a high-stakes clash at the Metropolitano Stadium.

“The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end,” Tuchel said.

“Absolutely brilliant. There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

“Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half. [Along] with everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.”

Asked whether Trafford had closed the gap to long-time No1 Pickford, Tuchel said: “[He was] very good. That is his job: to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.”

#1912. Man City guilty: Erling Haaland "answers" contract decision after verdict as Enzo Maresca faces January transfer problem

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 01:29

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has defended his choice to remain at Manchester City amid the fallout of their guilty verdict.

The Citizens were found guilty by an independent panel in September of breaching the Premier League's financial rules on an industrial scale.

A punishment has not yet been handed down, but there are fears among those associated with the club that sanctions could be as harsh as demotion.

It would be understandable if some players felt let down by City, who often expressed confidence that they would win their case.

Haaland revealed that he had no regrets about joining the club in 2022 and signing a new contract last year, telling TV2: "I assume the answers will come. I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it. To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

"A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022, and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I’m a City player and I’m incredibly happy there. I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022.

"We can all agree on that. I would say so myself when I look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're in the 1st seed pot for the Euro qualifiers. Things aren’t going so well for City in the league but we’ll try and turn that around against Fulham."

Haaland signed a new contract until 2034 in January 2025, though it is not clear if he would seek a move away from the club should they be severely punished.

City could win an appeal later this year, but the likelihood of the club overturning their guilty verdict is reportedly small.

A demotion to the Championship or lower divisions raises the possibility of a mass exodus, especially if the players have clauses in their contracts that make exits easier in the event of relegation.

Haaland is arguably the best striker in the world, and the 26-year-old will not want to spend at least a year of his prime competing for promotion.

It would not be surprising if the likes of Phil Foden or Nico O'Reilly opted to stay at the Etihad given they came through the academy, but it is hard to see others such as Haaland remaining a City player.

City currently find themselves third in the Premier League table, with the team trailing Arsenal by six points after 10 matchweeks.

Enzo Maresca will no doubt be targeting the January transfer window as an opportunity to strengthen in order to close the gap to the Gunners.

However, potential targets may be reluctant about joining the club due to the real threat of sanctions, and that would make a title challenge difficult.

#1910. Liverpool Confidential: Why Will Wright is the breakout star of Reds academy - LEWIS STEELE reveals club's plans for 6ft 3in hat-trick hero, his rise from Euxton Villa to Anfield and why coaches believe he's Andoni Iraola's next big thing

Published: 12:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 16:17 EST, 11 November 2026

On Will Wright’s last two trips abroad, he has needed to check in some extra baggage on the return flight.

Two UEFA Youth League away games, two hat-tricks and a pair of match balls to go with them. It’s now 13 goals for the season for 18-year-old Wright after his treble in a 5-3 win at Fenerbahce last week, and he has earned a first England youth call-up to boot.

Another hat-trick in one of those three games for the Young Lions? You wouldn’t bet against it – but Wright is used to these rapid rises.

Eighteen months ago, the 6ft 3in striker signed for Liverpool on a Friday, passed his driving test at 8am the next morning and then played for the first team the day after in a friendly at Anfield.

Now, the former Salford City striker is the name on everyone’s lips around Kirkby – with many thinking he could be the next cab off the rank from Liverpool’s famed academy.

Will Wright has lit up the academy goal charts this season for Liverpool, scoring a pair of hat-tricks in the UEFA Youth League

The Under 19s captain struck a brilliant treble against Fenerbahce last week to take his season tally to 13

Wright was first spotted by Salford scouts when playing for local side Euxton Villa, a ninth-tier club who have two England internationals among their alumni in David Unsworth and Sam Johnstone. Wright’s father, Mark, coached at Euxton and is an ex-professional for Preston North End.

It was an unusual path as most future stars are normally signed up by their mid-teens but Wright had injury issues amid a growth spurt that took him to the lanky frame that now bullies defenders. He had heel issues and has worked with a specialist on fascia problems.

Wright made his Salford debut in an 8-0 FA Cup defeat by Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City in January 2025 but scouts had already been alerted by his 50-goal haul at youth level. Arsenal, led by then-academy chief Per Mertesacker, launched an aggressive approach to sign him.

At one point, Liverpool signalled to Wright and Salford that they were pulling out of the deal, given Arsenal’s interest was so advanced. But the Reds soon returned to prevent the Gunners signing their next ‘Wrighty’.

The deal was worth peanuts in the grand scheme of things, around £300,000. It is good money for League Two Salford, though, and they will be set for additional payments for first-team appearances, honours and future national team caps.

Wright, who has a younger brother and is a Nike athlete, is a throwback No9. It is easy to reach for comparisons to current players but the way he combines pace, power and prolific finishing is not too dissimilar to Erling Haaland.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September, receiving possession on the touchline around halfway, tricking his way past two defenders and curling a sumptuous effort into the top corner.

He is the captain of the Under 19s team and I have watched him play live several times, including one game last season where he was clearly targeted by Atletico Madrid defenders. The striker was clattered, suffered a medial ligament injury and was sidelined for several months.

He is a strong dribbler and scored a fantastic solo goal for Liverpool's Under 21s against Rochdale in the EFL Trophy in September

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up

He has returned with a vengeance, with a hat-trick against LASK last month and then last week's effort against Fenerbahce. What impressed more in the latter was not his goals – one a penalty, the other two both true poachers’ finishes – but his assist.

Wright was on a hat-trick at the time but, instead of shooting, he played a ball to Finn Inglethorpe – son of academy director Alex – to score. Earlier, Wright and Josh Sonni-Lambie had argued over who was to take a penalty. Wright won the row and scored.

Under 21s boss Rob Page told the pair later that he would rather them show hunger to score and passion rather than shy away. Page is a huge fan of Wright and said: ‘There was a real maturity about his performance. One of the parts of the development for all the forwards is being unselfish in their actions.

‘As much as he wants to see the headlines and be successful himself, it is all about sharing that. Will has done that really well today with a hat-trick, a complete performance.’

Pressed on how far away Wright is from the first team, Page replied: ‘He doesn’t have to worry about that. Just bring the best version of yourself every day in training, give absolutely everything in games as he does. The rest will take care of itself.

‘He’s got a great support around him. His family are very supportive. Alex (Inglethorpe) is there to lean on, he’s got myself and Jay (Spearing, academy coach). He never gets carried away.’

Coaches have pinpointed hold-up play and heading as two things to work on, as well as instructing Wright not to ‘rise to the bait’ of bigger defenders who might try to ruffle him up. They have also worked on his off-the-ball runs to the back post.

So, what next? It is understood a January loan is being considered. Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons. His agent was at the AXA Training Centre on Tuesday and there will be no shortage of clubs willing to take him on.

Liverpool think toughening up Wright in a senior league could be a step worth taking, having used him in each of the last two pre-seasons

Wright got six minutes off the bench against Como in a friendly at Anfield in August, coming on for Alexander Isak up front

Andoni Iraola will be consulted, too. He has called up the likes of Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers this season and is eager to use young stars.

Iraola is in frequent dialogue with youth staff such as Page, Inglethorpe, plus Luiz Fernando Iubel who is often cited as the ‘link’ between the academy and first team.

The Brazilian has been spotted at several academy games this term, including for Wright’s hat-trick in Turkey where Iubel sat alongside sporting director Julian Ward and loans manager Gary Probert.

Whether a first-team breakthrough comes now or in the future, the future for Wright looks bright.

Dominik Szoboszlai’s participation with Hungary this week remains in the balance with the national team doing all they can to get their captain fit for crunch games.

The Hungarians take on Georgia and Northern Ireland in must-win Nations League matches – and may have to go without their star man. Szoboszlai hurt his knee in the win at Crystal Palace and, after an injury-hit six weeks, could do with a rest.

But he will try his best to be fit for national team duty and a decision will not be made until the 11th hour.

It comes after Virgil van Dijk pulled out of Dutch duty with a minor muscle issue. It is believed he has been managing the problem for at least a month and was surprised to be substituted on to the field against LASK — which might explain the team conceding three after he came on!

Virgil van Dijk (left) has pulled out of international duty and Dominik Szoboszlai (right) could be set to follow him

Confidential readers will recall our musings on Harvey Elliott a fortnight ago, with Valencia sources telling us that the La Liga outfit might consider cancelling his loan in January.

The English midfielder had struggled in Spain for fitness and form. He was then sent off against Villarreal but, as we reported, Valencia would give him another chance to prove his worth.

He has started well, scoring a free-kick in what was his first start for any club in 285 days. It was part of a notable 6-0 win in the Copa del Rey.

Elliott ran over to fans and put his arms aloft appearing to apologise, which adds to his comments a week ago about the red card where he said: ‘I made a mistake and I’m truly sorry. It won’t happen again.’

#1909. Mikel Arteta facing new Arsenal striker selection dilemma after inevitable Viktor Gyokeres goals

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Another Nations League appearance delivered the inevitable for Viktor Gyokeres.

His brace in Sweden’s 3-2 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina made it eight consecutive Nations League games in which he has scored, a record he holds by himself.

Whether Mikel Arteta spent his Saturday night tuned into the action from the Strawberry Arena is unclear, but we know exactly what his thoughts will have been.

Speaking after Gyokeres scored four goals in as many matches in the last international break, Arteta admitted: “Well, the first reaction is, ‘What am I doing that with me they don’t do this, or they haven’t been given the opportunity to do that?’

“That’s a natural one. But then you obviously are really happy.

“I’m very happy that they are able to help the national teams in that way, because I haven’t done it, but it should be one of the best feelings to represent your country and do it in such a way.”

Arteta, then, will be having the same reflections again. How does he get more of the Gyokeres in a Sweden shirt for Arsenal?

Win more penalties would be a good start. Both of Gyokeres’ goals against Bosnia came from the spot and he has now converted his last 29 penalties.

There is also the obvious caveat that the defences Gyokeres is coming up against at international level are not comparable to what he is facing for Arsenal.

As well as his two goals against Bosnia, Gyokeres assisted Alexander Isak’s finish. He ran in behind the high line and squared brilliantly for the Liverpool striker, though the strike was ruled out for offside.

It was perfect decision-making and execution but it was also the kind of space that Arsenal are not afforded on a regular basis.

The Champions League clash with Slavia Prague earlier this month, particularly in the first half, was a rare example of Arsenal being allowed to play with that freedom and Gyokeres delivered probably his best performance in an Arsenal shirt.

However, for all there are obvious tactical differences, the difference in performance levels when Gyokeres is playing for club rather than country is still alarmingly stark.

Gyokeres has had four shots in each of his last three Sweden appearances. Incredibly, he has managed a total of just four shots across 11 matches for Arsenal in the Premier League and Champions League this season.

It has often felt like a confidence issue. Gyokeres looks right at home when leading the line for Sweden. He is the main man, taking free-kicks, penalties, and constantly his team-mates are looking to find him.

The difference in performance levels when Gyokeres is playing for club rather than country is still alarmingly stark

Graham Potter has been important in that, emphasising at every opportunity just how crucial Gyokeres is to the team.

“He’s done brilliant for us when he’s been playing every week [for Arsenal], and he’s done brilliant for us when he hasn’t been playing every week,” Potter told The Independent ahead of this international break.

Gyokeres is not the main character at Arsenal. He knows Arteta will normally turn to Kai Havertz, especially in the big games, regardless of what form the German is in.

Havertz has struggled since picking up a hamstring issue in the last international break but he has still largely kept his place.

Even after Gyokeres played so well against Slavia and continued the big recent improvements in his hold-up play and combinations with those around him, he dropped back to the bench as Havertz started against Hull.

The striker debate is an ongoing one at Arsenal and on recent form, it feels as though the court of public opinion is edging back towards Gyokeres.

That is probably the biggest selection headache Arteta has ahead of Arsenal’s trip to face Newcastle on Saturday.

As the Arsenal boss has admitted himself, he is not getting as much out of Gyokeres as Potter is. For a perfectionist like Arteta, that will be a major source of frustration.

#1908. Greece vs Serbia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 02:13, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 05:04

Under pressure in League A of the UEFA Nations League, Greece will welcome Serbia to Panthessaliko Stadium for their final Group A2 showdown on Monday.

The Azure and White are battling for a place in the quarter-finals, while the Eagles are competing to earn a place in the League A/B playoffs.

Ivan Jovanovic's Greece kicked off their Nations League campaign in excellent fashion, but have been on a slow descent as the group has progressed.

The Azure and White beat Monday's opponents 2-1 in their opener on September 24, before claiming an impressive 1-0 victory over Germany three days later.

However, that success in Augsburg was Jovanovic's side's last taste of triumph, even if following it up with a pair of home draws against the Netherlands and Die Mannschaft was commendable.

On Friday, Greece were thrashed 7-0 by Xavi's Oranje, a defeat that was not only humiliating but has put their path to the quarter-finals in jeopardy.

Monday's hosts are currently second in Group A2, level on eight points with Germany, and must match their result while hoping Jurgen Klopp's team drop points on home soil in order to finish in the top two.

Meanwhile, Veljko Paunovic's Serbia have endured a disastrous Nations League term and are now fighting to avoid automatic demotion to League B, the fate awaiting the two lowest-ranked fourth-placed teams in League A.

The Eagles have lost all five of their matches so far, and are doomed to finish bottom of the group as a result, but they can still make the playoffs if they can rank higher than Turkey from Group A1 and the Czech Republic or Croatia from Group A3.

Paunovic's side are currently level on zero points with both Turkey and the Czech Republic, while boasting a three-superior goal-difference to those nations and a four-goal advantage over Croatia, who have three points.

Fans looking for a reason to be hopeful ahead of Monday's showdown could lean on the fact that Serbia were able to score in four of their defeats, three of which were by just one goal.

On the other hand, the Eagles were beaten 3-1 by Germany on Friday, falling two goals behind with just 14 minutes on the clock before having two players sent off in the second half.

That latest disappointment means the visitors have conceded 11 times in just five games - a rate of 2.2 per match - and their leaky defence could be exploited by a motivated Greece.

Greece are expected to be without midfielder Dimitrios Kourbelis due to an ankle injury, though Nectarios Triantis and Athanasios Androutsos should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Out wide, Arsenal's Christos Tzolis and Borussia Dortmund starboy Konstantinos Karetsas will be hoping to support a strike partnership of Vangelis Pavlidis and Fotis Ioannidis up top.

As for Serbia, they are missing Rangers midfielder Vanja Dragojevic and PAOK winger Andrija Zivkovic, both of whom are suspended after being sent off against Germany.

Filling the gaps, manager Paunovic could opt for Stefan Dzodic to be joined by Lazar Samardzic and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in midfield.

Further forward, Mihajlo Cvetkovic is likely to partner captain and record appearance holder Dusan Tadic in attack, desperate to fire his team into the playoffs.

Tzolakis; Rota, Mavropanos, Retsos, Tsimikas; Karetsas, Triantis, Androutsos, Tzolis; Pavlidis, Ioannidis

V Milinkovic-Savic; Nedeljkovic, Gudelj, Milenkovic, Babic, Sukacev; Samardzic, Dzodic, S Milinkovic-Savic; Cvetkovic, Tadic

Greece may have been hammered 7-0 by the Netherlands last time out, but that defeat came as a shock, and with a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the hosts will be motivated to bounce back.

Serbia have struggled throughout this term's Nations League, and it would be surprising to see them avoid a sixth consecutive defeat on Monday.

#1904. Ex-Premier League ref calls Mikel Arteta a ‘nightmare’ to deal with

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has named Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as the toughest person to deal with on the touchline.

Last month, Arteta received his second yellow card of the season during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton but said after the game that he had a dossier of other managers committing similar offences which have gone unpunished.

The Arsenal manager now faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives a third yellow card.

Scott, who refereed in the Premier League for a decade before retiring in 2025, claims Arteta ‘does push all the limits all of the time’ and described the Spaniard as ‘hard work’.

When asked who was the worst manager to deal with on the touchline, Scott told The Athletic: ‘Well, the trite answer is all of them when they’re losing.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The honest answer, I’m afraid, I know whatever I say at this point just gets me pelters but it is Arteta. He is the hardest work.

‘He really does push all the limits all of the time. I don’t mind that in many ways, he’s trying to get a competitive advantage for his team. That’s fine. That’s part of his job. And of course, he’s entitled to do it, and it’s for us to place them, but he does make your life extremely difficult.

‘He’s out of his box [technical area] all the time. I watched him recently in the game against Everton and every time Everton had the ball anywhere near the touchline on his side, he was like joining in the press, his toes are on the touchline.

‘As fourth official, it’s a nightmare, because if you step forward and do anything about it, you’re being pedantic, being petty. He does get away with rather too much. The officials do need to be a bit tighter. And I was one of them who let him do that. I’m not going to deny that. But he was just hard work. Really, really hard work all the time in a way that others tended to be hard work some of the time.

Manchester United’s alternative targets to Mauricio Pochettino have been revealed.

During the autumn international break, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2018/19.

While City deny any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal, serious sanctions - such as points deductions, fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League - are likely if that fails.

Bassey is approaching the final six months of his contract at Fulham, so could be available for a cut-price fee.

Belgium manager Rudi Garcia has revealed that he had two interviews at Manchester United about taking over as the club’s manager.

He told The Athletic: “I’d like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough.

“It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf [Rangnick].”

#1902. Arsenal: Viktor Gyokeres overtakes Cristiano Ronaldo, extends all-time Nations League goals record

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 07:35

Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres extended an extraordinary UEFA Nations League goals record and surpassed Cristiano Ronaldo in Sweden's 3-2 victory over Bosnia-Herzegovina on Saturday evening.

The 28-year-old has experienced a frustrating start to the 2026-27 season with Arsenal, scoring just two goals in 14 appearances, while also providing three assists.

Gyokeres has started just one Premier League game to boot, having fallen behind Kai Havertz in the strikers' pecking order, but he remains indispensable for the Sweden national team.

Gyokeres and strike partner Alexander Isak led the line for Graham Potter's men against Bosnia, whom Sweden drew first blood against through Daniel Svensson with just five minutes gone.

Gyokeres doubled his nation's lead from the penalty spot shortly afterwards, before rifling home from 12 yards yet again on the stroke of half time, and Sweden survived a fightback attempt from their visitors to make it four wins from five.

By making the net bulge at the Strawberry Arena, Gyokeres scored for the eighth Nations League game running, becoming the first player in the history of the competition to achieve that feat.

Viktor Gyökeres has now scored in eight consecutive Nations League games for Sweden ?? 8 games played, 12 goals ? https://t.co/jOt5Hc5U6o

The 28-year-old already held the record for the most consecutive Nations League games scored in, as no other player has struck in more than six straight matches.

However, Gyokeres has now extended his unparalleled achievement; his closest challenger is England captain Harry Kane, who has scored in six consecutive Nations League matches and could make it seven on the spin when the Three Lions face Spain on Sunday.

Gyokeres's record run began in October 2024, when he netted once in a 3-0 win over Serbia, and the ex-Sporting Lisbon man also bagged against Slovakia and Azerbaijan in that year's tournament, scoring four against the latter.

Gyokeres now boasts six goals from five Nations League games in 2026-27, scoring in previous matches against Romania, Bosnia, Poland and Romania again before his Saturday double.

Not only did Gyokeres's brace on Saturday extend his successive scoring streak; the Arsenal forward has now overtaken Cristiano Ronaldo in the all-time Nations League scoring charts.

Ronaldo managed 15 Nations League goals for Portugal, but Gyokeres has now found the net 16 times in the competition, the second-most in the competition's history.

The Sweden star now only trails Erling Haaland in the list, as the Manchester City marksman has scored 23 Nations League goals for Norway after his strike in Saturday's victory over Wales.

Sweden have now moved onto 13 points from five games in League B Group 4, thus guaranteeing promotion to League A ahead of their last game against Poland on Tuesday.

#1900. GdS: Club Brugge name price for Tresoldi – why a difficult negotiation beckons for Milan

AC Milan have already discovered the starting price for Nicolo Tresoldi, and it’s safe to say it will not be a cheap deal.

According to this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), it is no secret that Tresoldi sits at the top of the wish list for Milan. Gerry Cardinale, first and foremost, is a big admirer of the rising Brugge star.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is equally well-known that the striker has been a lifelong fan of the Rossoneri. However, his contract runs until 2029, so to take him away from the Jan Breydel Stadium a negotiation is needed with a club that are tough to deal with, as the past shows.

The phone lines between Milan and Brugge were first used in 2022, when the Charles De Ketelaere saga took place. Since then, the management teams at both Milan and the Belgian club have changed, but the history between the two sides should help facilitate discussions. Ardon Jashari was another arduous negotiation, but one that eventually reached the finish line too.

In the cases of De Ketelaere and Jashari, the pitch has arguably favoured the seller more than the buyer. Perhaps the outcome will be different with Tresoldi, should the two parties actually sit down to negotiate.

One caveat: especially in January, the asking is bound to be significant. How significant? Around €60m, according to whispers from Flanders.

Club Brugge are accustomed to selling their best players when the time comes, but they are under no pressure to do so, especially while the season is still underway. Tresoldi has effectively carried the team on his back, scoring eight goals in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Super Cup.

The total: 14 goals in 17 official matches. For the club to part ways with their star striker during the mid-season window – a time when all their competitive objectives remain within reach – the offer would certainly need to be more than substantial.

Furthermore, if the 22-year-old forward maintains his current scoring rate throughout the season, his market value will only continue to climb. It is a risk, but also an opportunity. Moreover, Milan are not alone in the race for Tresoldi.

Bayern Munich and top English clubs are keeping a close eye on the former Hannover man, who was born in Cagliari but is a key player for the German U21 national team. Consequently, if Cardinale wishes to beat the competition, he would need to act quickly and decisively.

He demonstrated he can dothis over the summer with the signings of Gonçalo Ramos, Diego Moreira, and Mario Gila. However, authorising a €60m expenditure would require the right conditions: specifically, Milan must be in the hunt for a major objective.

Tresoldi’s arrival could not see him then become a back-up to Gonçalo Ramos, the most expensive signing in the club’s history. In essence, it requires Ruben Amorim to provide the necessary assurances regarding the wisdom of the acquisition.

Meanwhile, Tresoldi’s hat-trick against Inter at San Siro on October 13th in the Champions League has naturally excited the Rossoneri fans, who would be more than happy to embrace him. However, they aren’t the ones who have to pay the €60m.

#1899. Arsenal star ‘will not turn down Real Madrid’ when transfer offer comes

Arsenal star William Saliba would not turn down a move to Real Madrid, according to his former teammate Morgan Schneiderlin.

Saliba has developed into one of the best centre-halves in world football under Mikel Arteta having arrived from Saint-Etienne for £27million in 2019.

During his time in north London, the centre-half has been persistently linked with a move to Real Madrid. Last year, Mikel Arteta sat down with his defender to discuss the ‘noise’ with Saliba telling the Gunners boss he was happy in north London.

Former Southampton, Manchester United and Everton midfielder Schneiderlin played alongside the France international for one season at Nice back in 2021, convinced then of his world class ability.

But the former Premier League star feels there will come a time where he will be unable to say no to a move to the Bernabeu.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘William Saliba to Real Madrid? That’s something he will need to decide for himself,’ Schneiderlin told ComeOn.

‘It’s not for me to say whether he should stay at Arsenal or go to Madrid but what I do know, having played alongside him, is that he is a top centre-back with an elite mentality who always wants to improve.

‘He’s coming back from a long injury now, but I think the bigger question is actually for Arsenal: if you lose Saliba, who do you replace him with?

‘There are very few centre-backs in the world right now capable of delivering those kinds of performances.

‘I said this many years ago when he was playing for Nice, if I were a big club, I would buy him immediately, because down the line his price tag would become far too high.

‘He is an incredible player to have in your side. But when a decision like that comes up, there are a handful of clubs in your career that you simply cannot turn down, and Real Madrid is one of them.’

Saliba returned to action before the international break having recovered from a back problem and will hope to start when Arsenal resume their Premier League campaign away to Newcastle on 21 November.

#1898. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.
